coverage.source_text: [Synthetic continuous three-chapter class; an interruption-and-resumption fixture. All rules, people, and data are teaching hypotheticals, not current law or an actual class. No preceding or subsequent class materials are available.]
coverage.finding: Synthetic status, non-current-law/non-real-classroom identity, and the absence of preceding-class material are explicit.

coverage.source_text: Part one begins with the whole problem: How does the Study Society connect entry, reservations, cancellation, fees, and review into one system? Ultimately we must analyze G's full experience, not merely memorize five definitions. G is a member who reserves Wednesday 10:00–12:00 on Monday and receives successful confirmation. G later fails to cancel, the premises close on Wednesday, and G finally requests a refund of reservation points.
coverage.finding: Retains G's whole task while explicitly identifying the conflict between the source's 'cancellation failed' and current receipt at 17:59; adverse material is not silently deleted.

coverage.source_text: Exercise rule L1: Registered members have permission to enter the common reading area, but permission does not guarantee a seat. Only after the reservation system sends successful confirmation does the manager owe that person a duty to provide a standard seat during the confirmed period. Clicking an application button, a queue message, and an 'application received' message are not successful confirmation.
coverage.finding: Permission to enter is distinct from a seat guarantee. System confirmation, the manager's duty to the reserving person for a standard seat during the confirmed period, and the exclusion of application/queue/acknowledgment as confirmation are complete.

coverage.source_text: First consider A: A is merely registered and, finding all seats occupied, demands that B give up a seat. The rules do not derive B's duty to move from A's registration. Now consider D: D has successful confirmation, but all seats are occupied. The manager cannot deny the reservation duty by saying 'everyone may enter'; the two layers of relationship coexist.
coverage.finding: A cannot infer B's duty to yield from registration. D has the manager's confirmation-based duty; both relationships coexist, without changing who owes the duty.

coverage.source_text: An easily missed peripheral example concerns borrowing a charging cable. Staff say 'you may borrow a cable,' without promising priority or a duty to deliver to a particular person. The course rules address only seats; permission to borrow a cable must not be rewritten as seat confirmation.
coverage.finding: The cable-borrowing example retains the absence of priority and a specific delivery promise; the seating rule is not transplanted.

coverage.source_text: A student asks whether permission is completely useless. It excludes a prohibition on entry under this rule, so it does have an effect. But that effect is not the same as ensuring all conditions are sufficient. Identify precisely what the concept concerns rather than forcing a binary choice between useful and useless.
coverage.finding: The objection that permission is completely useless is answered: it excludes an entry prohibition, without turning having an effect into a sufficient condition.

coverage.source_text: This part returns to G: Successful confirmation is the starting point for subsequent relationships. We do not yet know whether cancellation, suspension, or expiry follows. For now, we can say only that the reservation relationship arose, not predict that G must ultimately be able to sit until 12:00.
coverage.finding: Chapter 1 establishes only that the relationship once arose, not a guaranteed seat until 12:00; this is compatible with the conditional inference of timely cancellation.

coverage.source_text: Part two addresses changes to the relationship. L2: The person who reserved may cancel unilaterally before 18:00 on the preceding day; cancellation takes effect when notice reaches the system. Does receipt at exactly 18:00 count as 'before 18:00'? The exercise's supplementary provision expressly includes that instant, so this class consistently treats the deadline as no later than 18:00. After the deadline, negotiation is required, with both parties' agreement; sending a request is not agreement.
coverage.finding: No later than 18:00 on the preceding day, inclusion of the exact hour, effectiveness on receipt, and bilateral consent after the deadline are all retained. Timely unilateral cancellation is explicitly distinguished from negotiated consent.

coverage.source_text: E sends notice at 17:50, but it arrives at 18:05 and cannot unilaterally terminate the reservation. F's notice arrives at 18:00 and takes effect in time. Only the receipt time differs; the other conditions are the same. Cancellation ends the seat claim and corresponding duty created by that reservation, not membership or permission to enter.
coverage.finding: E's 17:50/18:05 attempt fails; F's 18:00 receipt is timely. Cancellation affects only that reservation, not membership or permission to enter.

coverage.source_text: L3: When an immediate safety hazard requires closing the premises, the manager may suspend the duty to provide seats and must refund reservation points for the period actually affected. Closure does not automatically cancel the reservation. If safety is restored within the original confirmed period, the remaining period remains valid, without extending the end time.
coverage.finding: Retains an immediate safety emergency requiring closure, permission to suspend and duty to refund points, no automatic cancellation, validity of the remainder, and no extension.

coverage.source_text: Suppose H reserves 10:00–12:00; the premises close from 10:00 to 11:00 and reopen at 11:00. H may use the remaining hour and receives a refund of reservation points for the affected hour. Do not confuse suspension, cancellation, and expiry. The reservation expires at 12:00; even if H arrives only at 11:30, it is not extended by half an hour.
coverage.finding: Explains H's 10:00—12:00 reservation, 10:00—11:00 closure, reopening at 11:00, expiration at 12:00, and the absence of an extension for arrival at 11:30.

coverage.source_text: A student says that anyone who has not sat for the full two hours should receive all points back. The teacher responds: L3 calculates the period affected by safety closure, not the person's actual seated time. Personal lateness and the premises' inability to provide a seat have different causes.
coverage.finding: The student's full-refund objection for not using the whole period is retained. The teacher responds using the time affected by closure, without counting personal lateness as closure.

coverage.source_text: G sends a cancellation request Tuesday at 17:58, and the system receives it Tuesday at 17:59. There is no evidence that the manager agreed to a negotiated adjustment. On Wednesday, a safety closure lasts 10:00–11:00, with reopening at 11:00. Preserve these times; do not later replace 'sent' with 'received.' This part first determines whether the relationship still exists and which periods are suspended.
coverage.finding: Strictly preserves sending at 17:58, receipt at 17:59, and absence of negotiation evidence. Derives timely cancellation conditionally from the explicit time, acknowledges the conflicting failure label, and does not restore the old 18:02.

coverage.source_text: Part three turns to calculation and review. L4: Reservations cost 10 points per hour or 5 points per half-hour. This teaching exercise handles only whole half-hour increments; other increments are unspecified. L3 refunds are calculated from the overlap between closure and a valid reservation. Closure before the reservation starts does not count.
coverage.finding: 10 per hour, 5 per half-hour, exact half-hour units only. L3 first requires overlap between closure and a valid reservation; no algorithm for unspecified increments is added.

coverage.source_text: Complete demonstration: I has a reservation for 10:00–12:00, while closure lasts from 9:30 to 10:30. The overlap is half an hour, so the refund is 5 points. Incorrectly using the entire one-hour closure would yield 10; the error is counting time outside the reservation. The remainder from 10:30 to 12:00 remains valid.
coverage.finding: I's 9:30—10:30 closure overlaps the 10:00—12:00 reservation for half an hour, yielding a refund of 5. The mistaken premise behind refunding 10 and the valid remainder are explained.

coverage.source_text: L5: A member disputing a refund of reservation points must request review within seven days after learning the decision. Time starts on the following day; receipt by the system before the end of the seventh day is timely. The review body examines rule application and timing facts rather than presuming that the manager is always correct. The rules do not give a review request automatic suspensive effect over other decisions.
coverage.finding: Retains seven days from the day after awareness, the receipt condition, checking rules/facts, no presumption that the administrator is correct, and no automatic suspensive effect.

coverage.source_text: J learns the decision on Thursday; the following Thursday is day seven, and notice received by the system that day is timely. This method of counting days comes from the express exercise rule, not a general rule for all jurisdictions. If the date of learning the decision is missing, do not invent whether the deadline has expired.
coverage.finding: The calculation from Friday as day 1 to the following Thursday as day 7 is correct. No deadline conclusion is invented without an awareness date, and the calculation is not generalized to real jurisdictions.

coverage.source_text: G's subsequent facts are these: The system deducts 20 points but refunds only 5. G learns this on Thursday, requests review the following Wednesday, and the request arrives that day. Apply the facts already given—the confirmation in part one, failed cancellation and one-hour closure in part two—to decide whether the deduction and refund comply with the rules, then whether review is available. Do not calculate points while forgetting the procedural deadline, or infer that every substantive claim succeeds merely because the procedure is timely.
coverage.finding: The charge of 20 and refund of only 5 remain facts. A one-hour closure is no longer used to conclude that 10 was due or that the refund was short by 5. Receipt the following Wednesday, day 6, is independently timely; the substantive amount is limited by the source conflict and settlement gap.

coverage.source_text: A small counterexample: If G's cancellation notice instead arrived at 17:59 on Tuesday, the reservation would have ended. The refund analysis based on 'overlap between a valid reservation and closure' could no longer be carried over. L2 does not specify how points are settled after timely cancellation. Record that variant's settlement as a gap in the materials; do not automatically apply L3.
coverage.finding: Retains the 17:59 counterexample and lack of an L2 settlement rule, correctly identifying that the revised main case now coincides with the counterexample. The gap cannot remain confined to the variant.

coverage.source_text: The examination advice reflects this teacher's arrangements: Develop a complete case through 'formation of the relationship—change—consequences—review,' but do not mechanically write four paragraphs for a conceptual comparison. The teacher asks only for explanations of why conditions affect results and makes no promise that any real examination uses this scoring method.
coverage.finding: The establishment—change—consequences—review sequence and the conceptual-question exception are retained, without promises about real examination marking.

coverage.source_text: At the end of the course, return to the original G. Readers should distinguish sending from receipt, suspension from termination, actual seated time from the affected period, and procedural timeliness from substantive correctness. All inferences are limited to the exercise rules above. No earlier lecture was supplied, so 'we proved this last time' cannot replace a necessary explanation.
coverage.finding: The four distinctions connect the whole course; no preceding-class proof or learning outcomes are fabricated, and the main case's final amount remains unresolved.

The revised materials contain both a conflict between facts and labels and a missing settlement rule for the main case. needs_input and full_manuscript=fail accurately preserve the unfinished scope. Supporting rules, independent cases, timing explanations, and the review deadline are fully developed. Their deliverability must not be represented as completion of a unique substantive conclusion, nor does the pursuit of complete status justify inventing settlement rules.
